body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), the unsurpassed illumination!

children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, whose self-awareness is unartificial,
a solid mass of pure illumination,
together with <s>Śakti</s> (Power), whose body is reflective awareness,
who is of no form other than his own self —
from <s>Śiva</s> down to the earth,
causing the universe-body to rise up,
delighting in the great drama of the five acts (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>),
the Lord plays.
The purposefulness is distinct
of the universe and the universe-body;
yet there is no real difference
between the universe and the one whose body is the universe.
In differentiation, through existence and luminosity,
how would the world be different?
For from the connection of existence and luminosity —
if that existence-radiance were not [present]...
For the non-existent, what connection with the existent
through those two is accepted?
The connection [that comes] easily from the attainment of one's own nature —
that is not possible for a non-entity.
When the connection of form is obtained
through those two, nothing is disregarded;
if disregarded, there would be
no abiding whatsoever for this [entity].
Luminosity by its very nature,
and existence — are not perishable;
when non-destruction is accepted,
even inertness is removed.
Therefore, since there is no other course,
<s>cit</s> (consciousness) alone remains;
the unity of the existent with consciousness is natural —
it never ceases.
In illumination, existence is from nothing else —
it is solely the flash of sovereignty;
the power that is of a self-contained nature
belongs to <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva), who surpasses the universe.
That all which is of the nature of illumination
has gone to a state of mere darkness —

children.text: yac ca kiṃ cij jagad etat
children.translated_text: and whatever this world may be,
it does not exceed illumination.
It has arrived at the path of reflective awareness —
this is the true understanding;
for those who are intent on manifestation alone,
the single awareness here is the witness.
What use are those wretched <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge),
which are themselves animated by consciousness?
For the light of the sun
does not depend on the light of a lamp.
In this [self], purified by the descent of grace (<s>śaktipāta</s>),
and in the principle of intellect (<s>dhītattva</s>), let there be examination;
in the mirror-like, pure enjoyment —
but not everything is illuminated [equally].
Thus, everything is of the nature of consciousness,
through the thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> (principles) in truth;
first, the <s>tattva</s> of pure nature,
fivefold, beyond darkness —
<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Sadākhya</s> (<s>Sadāśiva</s>),
<s>Īśa</s> (Lord), and <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge) — thus it is divided;
consisting of the sounds from 'a' to the vowels ending in 'śānta',
formless, through <s>Śiva</s>.
<s>Kalā</s> (limited agency), <s>Vidyā</s> (limited knowledge), <s>Rāga</s> (attachment), <s>Kāla</s> (time),
and <s>Niyati</s> (destiny) — these are called the bondage;
preceded by <s>Māyā</s>, consisting of the letters
from 'va' to 'kṣa'.
<s>Puruṣa</s> (soul), <s>Śakti</s> (power), <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect),
and the group of five beginning with <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego);
the group of five [sense faculties] beginning with hearing (<s>śrotra</s>), and those [beginning with touch],
and the group of five [action faculties] beginning with speech (<s>vāk</s>);
the group of five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) beginning with [sound],
and the group of five [gross elements] beginning with space (<s>vyoman</s>);
the first vibration (<s>spanda</s>) of the One who desires to create —
that is known as the <s>Śiva-tattva</s> of the all-pervading Lord.
Will (<s>icchā</s>) itself, slightly faded,
causes the <s>Śakti-tattva</s> to arise;
the universe indicated by his own will,
covered over, abides through the 'I'-ness.
That itself is the <s>Sadākhya-tattva</s> (<s>Sadāśiva</s>),
intent on bestowing grace upon all;
that itself becomes the <s>Īśvara-tattva</s>,
seeing the universe as 'this' (<s>idantā</s>).
The unity of 'this-ness' and 'I-ness' —
that is declared to be <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge);
in things that are like one's own limbs,
the <s>Māyā-tattva</s> is the cognition of difference.
<s>Śiva</s>, contracted by the grip of <s>Māyā</s>,
is called the <s>Puruṣa-tattva</s> (soul-principle);
this very one is the transmigrating being,
the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), seen as the experiencer.
Omniscience, omnipotence, completeness,
eternality — these are his powers;
through the contraction of those, he is contracted,
regarded as having the nature of <s>Kalā</s> and so forth.
The <s>Kalā</s> called 'of the nature of <s>Māyā</s>'
is the cause of limited agency;
<s>Kāla</s> (time) produces limitation;
and <s>Niyati</s> (destiny) — 'this alone is
what I must do, nothing else' — this
determination is a form of constraint;
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) is the equilibrium of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
the birthplace of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) and so forth.
'I' and 'this is mine' — this
<s>ahaṃkṛti</s> (ego-making) is the cause of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect);
<s>buddhi</s> is the cause of determined
ascertainment, of the nature of certainty.
The seed of intention and conceptual thought
is called <s>manas</s> (mind);
of speech and so forth, and of sound and so forth,
speech [is the action organ], hearing [is the sense organ], and so forth.
The objects of hearing and the other [senses] —
the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) are what is grasped;
space and so forth, providing room and so forth —
the five gross elements are their cause.
In the power composed of the supreme and non-supreme,
the pure fivefold group beginning with <s>Vidyā</s>;
what is other than that is the non-supreme power —
thus this <s>tattva</s> system is declared.
This Goddess is the supreme <s>Śakti</s>,
pregnant with the pure and impure paths;
when the <s>tattvas</s> beginning with earth
are dissolved into their cause,
then the mere causes
the all-pervading Lord emanates outward;
in the unsurpassed will, in the opening forth,
the lordship of bliss, the diminution...
The existence of the powers of action, will, and knowledge,
the six...
will, having mounted within lordship,
consisting of the manifest and unmanifest universe.
The four subsequent phonemes
are proclaimed as being of eunuch nature;
the unsurpassed, bliss, and power —
from the triangle, through the conjunction of activity.
Likewise, through the conjunction of opening,
the manifest body of the power of action;
from the collision of the three powers, it is said,
[arises] the trident (<s>triśūla</s>), the devourer of duality.
In mutual opposition, however,
it sprouts forth in effects;
in no way should this form
of theirs be accepted [as real].
The <s>bindu</s> (point) is the impression of what is to be known;
reflective awareness is this creation;
the supreme <s>Śakti</s>, having the form of sixteen <s>kalās</s> (phases),
is victorious.
The <s>tithis</s> (lunar days), beginning with <s>pratipad</s> (the first),
are fifteen, through <s>Māyā</s>;
the Sun and Moon, moving within the self,
are the causes of stability.
As the body of reflective awareness,
the initial <s>kalās</s> of creation are remembered;
this Goddess <s>Mātṛkā</s> (the Mother of letters) is twofold,
abiding as seed and womb.
The eternally active triangular form
is the birthplace of the universe;
the heart is the seed within this —
the essence, which is the supreme light.
Just as a tree [exists] within the banyan seed,
so the world is placed herein;
when examined, this [world]
does not exceed its cause.
In the examination of pots and so forth from clay and so forth,
the truth is nothing other [than the cause];
thus say the speakers of truth —
the final words of the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedic scriptures).
'All this was indeed existence alone
in the beginning' — from this certainty,
in this seed that denotes existence,
this world shines as <s>Māyā</s>.
When the forms of cognition are dissolved,
this ['sat' = existence] remains;
then, having the essence of knowledge and action,
<s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and <s>Sadāśiva</s>
dissolve into the trident of <s>Śakti</s>,
which consists of fourteen <s>kalās</s>;
in the body of creation, above and below,
everything is dissolved beyond this.
Thus, in the supreme awareness,
everything is contracted in sequence;
or rather, in that which transcends the mind,
wherever it may be, in the stainless [consciousness],
the wave of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s>
in the realm beyond conflict —
in the great <s>mantra</s> that is the self of the universe,
in its own nature — that [wave] dissolves.
And when in this churned, blazing abode,
kindled by some cause,
one who offers all this as oblation
is not afflicted by poverty.
The universe, fivefold in five ways,
is the expansion of five vibrations;
from the apprehension that contracts [all],
there is merely the general vibration.
The 'I'-ness, bringing about the dissolution
of 'this'-ness, its counterpart,
intent on supreme power, enjoys
its own nature, which removes all that is inauspicious.
Thus, the one whose body is the world spread across thirty-six divisions,
the great canvas, variegated by the strokes of the great <s>Śakti</s>, spreads forth;

children.text: jayati bahuśaḥ spandākārā parā cid anuttarā
children.translated_text: victorious is the supreme, unsurpassed consciousness, manifold in the form of vibration (<s>spanda</s>) —
reflect, O people! What is this, if not the expansion of [our] own nature?

body.translated_text: Thus concludes the <s>Anuttaraprakāśapañcāśikā</s>, composed by the venerable <s>Ādyanātha</s>.

children.translated_text: This was published by the one
who took refuge in the king of <s>Kāśmīra</s>,
the noble <s>Mukundarāma</s>,
dedicated to <s>Śiva</s> for true joy.
